## Proof

We work in $C[0,1]$ with the supremum norm $\|f\|=\max_{0\le x\le 1}|f(x)|$. The operator is

$$Af(x)=\int_0^1 K(x,y)f(y)\,dy,\qquad K(x,y)=x.$$

Since $K(x,y)=x$ is independent of $y$,

$$Af(x)=x\int_0^1 f(y)\,dy.$$

**Upper bound.** For any $f\in C[0,1]$,

$$|Af(x)|=\left|x\int_0^1 f(y)\,dy\right|\le x\int_0^1 |f(y)|\,dy\le x\int_0^1 \|f\|\,dy=x\|f\|.$$

Taking the maximum over $x\in[0,1]$ (and using $x\le 1$),

$$\|Af\|=\max_{0\le x\le 1}|Af(x)|\le \max_{0\le x\le 1}x\cdot\|f\|=\|f\|.$$

Thus $\|A\|\le 1$.

**Lower bound.** Take the constant function $f\equiv 1$, which has $\|f\|=1$. Then

$$Af(x)=x\int_0^1 1\,dy=x,$$

so $\|Af\|=\max_{0\le x\le 1}x=1$. Therefore

$$\|A\|\ge \frac{\|Af\|}{\|f\|}=1.$$

Combining both bounds,

$$\boxed{\|A\|=1}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
